title: Kashmir's Owais Yaqoob Stuns Unbeaten Delyan Georgiev With First-Round TKO in Bulgaria
excerpt: The 24-year-old Khabib Nurmagomedov protégé from Pulwama extended his winning streak to six fights, stopping the Bulgarian hometown favorite at Brave CF 107 in Burgas.
body:
• Owais Yaqoob defeated previously unbeaten Delyan Georgiev via TKO (punches) at 4:00 of Round 1 at Brave CF 107 in Burgas, Bulgaria on August 1
  • The Kashmiri fighter, who trains under Khabib Nurmagomedov's system in Russia, improved his record to 6-1 and extended his winning streak to six consecutive bouts
  • Yaqoob overcame visa delays and fought as a heavy underdog — 73% of Tapology community picks favored Georgiev — in front of the Bulgarian's home crowd

Kashmiri MMA fighter Owais Yaqoob pulled off one of the biggest upsets on the Brave CF circuit this year, stopping previously undefeated Bulgarian prospect Delyan Georgiev via TKO in the first round at Brave CF 107 at the Arena Burgas on August 1.

Yaqoob, fighting at a 150-pound catchweight, ended the contest with a barrage of punches at the 4:00 mark of the opening round. The victory improved his professional record to 6-1 and marked his fourth first-round stoppage in seven career fights.

Underdog Walks Into Hostile Territory

The odds were stacked against the 24-year-old from Pulwama, Kashmir. Georgiev (3-1), a two-time IMMAF World Champion, was undefeated heading into the bout and fighting in his home country. The Tapology community overwhelmingly favored the Bulgarian, with 73% of 185 fan predictions backing Georgiev to win.

https://x.com/GreaterKashmir/status/2084228284884373643

Yaqoob's path to the cage was itself uncertain. Visa complications threatened to keep him out of the event for several days before a last-minute clearance allowed him to travel to Bulgaria, according to FightBook MMA.

"Delyan Georgiev is a young and talented fighter from Bulgaria, so I know this will be a tough test in front of his supporters. These are the kind of fights that push you to the next level, and I'm ready for it."

— Owais Yaqoob, pre-fight interview with FightBook MMA

From Thang Ta to the Global Stage

Yaqoob's trajectory is unlike most fighters on the international MMA circuit. Before transitioning to mixed martial arts, he won four Indian national championships in Thang Ta, one of India's oldest traditional martial arts originating from Manipur.

He later relocated to Russia to train at the Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov School, the facility built by the late father of former UFC lightweight champion Khabib Nurmagomedov. That training pedigree has become a defining element of Yaqoob's career — his grappling-heavy, pressure-based style mirrors the approach that made Nurmagomedov one of the most dominant fighters in UFC history.

The matchup at Brave CF 107 carried an added layer of intrigue: Georgiev trained alongside UFC featherweight champion Ilia Topuria, making the bout a proxy clash between two of modern MMA's most respected championship systems.

A Streak Built on Finishes

The win over Georgiev was Yaqoob's sixth consecutive victory and his third straight first-round stoppage under the Brave CF banner. At Brave CF 98 in Zhengzhou, China in September 2025, he stopped Ian Paul Lora via strikes in the first round. Three months later at Brave CF 103 in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, he finished Mehmet Can Tasdoven with a knee and punches in just 1:24.

Those performances earned Yaqoob the 2025 Brave CF Breakout Fighter of the Year award, according to the promotion. He is currently ranked sixth among lightweights in South Asia on Tapology.

What It Means for the Diaspora

India, with nearly 1.5 billion people, remains one of the largest untapped markets in global MMA. While cricket and football dominate the sports landscape, fighters like Yaqoob are carving out a niche that resonates with young Indians at home and abroad.

Back in Pulwama, Yaqoob runs the Lions Den Martial Arts Academy, which has become a training hub for aspiring combat sports athletes in Kashmir — a region more traditionally associated with cricket, football, and winter sports.

"This is more than just a fight — it's history for Kashmir."

— Owais Yaqoob

What's Next

With six wins and a growing reputation as one of Asia's most exciting young fighters, Yaqoob is positioning himself for bigger opportunities within Brave CF's lightweight division. The promotion's next event, Brave CF 108, is scheduled for September 5 in Pula, Croatia. Whether Yaqoob features on that card remains to be seen, but his trajectory suggests a title shot may not be far off.
